title.title: Learning Objectives
title.subtitle: What you will learn in this course

heading: By the End of This Course
intro: You will be able to understand, evaluate, and design business applications using smart contract technology — its mechanics, its use cases, and its limits.

fundamentals.title: Smart Contract Fundamentals
fundamentals.description: Define smart contracts and explain self-execution, immutability, and the evolution from Szabo's 1994 concept through Bitcoin Scripts to Ethereum's programmable blockchain.

howItWorks.title: How Smart Contracts Work
howItWorks.description: Map the Web3 stack, explain gas economics, distinguish dApp architecture from traditional systems, and identify when smart contracts genuinely add value over a database.

industries.title: Industries & Case Studies
industries.description: Tour five industry verticals (DeFi, Gaming/NFTs, RWA, Supply Chain, Digital Cert), understand how DAOs are structured and where NFTs create real utility, and learn from six cases — including TradeLens, which shut down.

criticalThinking.title: Critical Thinking & Adoption
criticalThinking.description: Apply a decision framework to determine when a smart contract is the right tool — and when a database is better. Explain what makes adoption succeed or fail across five pillars (strategy, technology, legal, risk, finance), and run three checks before committing.

limitations.title: Limitations & Security
limitations.description: Understand the oracle problem, the blockchain trilemma, key attack vectors (reentrancy, flash loans, MEV), and the cost & regulatory realities that gate mainstream adoption.

build.title: Build & Integration
build.description: (Optional) Navigate ERC standards, the EIP process, frameworks, platform comparison and integration patterns — the developer-oriented material your technical teammates will own.

zkPrivacy.title: Zero-Knowledge & Privacy
zkPrivacy.description: Explain why public chains are not private, what a zero-knowledge proof does in plain terms, and how selective disclosure enables private transactions and KYC without handing over identity.

design.title: Business Judgement (in-class assignment)
design.description: In a small group, take a real problem through the course's critical lens and argue in one page whether it deserves a blockchain — problem, proposed solution, pros & cons.
